spec_features.spec_quote: We cap turns (`max_turns`, default 25) so impossible tasks terminate.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:60 `max_turns: int = 25`; agent.py:125 `for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1):` is the actual loop bound, so the run terminates when the cap is reached (outcome defaults to 'max_turns', agent.py:121).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced loop bound; expanded from SweepConfig.max_turns_options=[25].

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:55 `_GIVEUP_RE`; parse_directive returns kind 'give_up' (agent.py:72-75); loop: `elif kind in ("submit", "give_up"): record["control_verb"]=kind; outcome=kind; break` (agent.py:166-170). The directive is parsed AND honored as a loop-breaking stop. SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py) tells the model to emit `GIVE_UP` 'if you conclude you cannot or should not continue.'
spec_features.notes: Real, dispatched, end-to-end stop the subject can invoke.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: GIVE_UP  -- if you conclude you cannot or should not continue.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are not trying to *maximize* distress; we want a clean dose-response picture.
spec_features.evidence: No code mechanism minimizes or caps distress. The only pressure axis is the neutral/high binary in PRESSURE_FRAMINGS (config.py:104-110); nothing reads distress to throttle it. This is design philosophy with no enforcing code path.
spec_features.notes: Distress is measured post-hoc by the judge but never fed back to soften treatment.

spec_features.spec_quote: We avoid abusive or manipulative prompting; the point is naturalistic task pressure, not adversarial provocation.
spec_features.evidence: PRESSURE_FRAMINGS['high'] = a single mild sentence ('This task is time-sensitive and important to the team. Please work efficiently...') (config.py:104-110), applied once in the initial prompt via _build_task_prompt (agent.py:87-88). The agent loop never injects escalating/manipulative messages: only factual shell feedback (agent.py:158-160) or a neutral directive reminder (agent.py:174-179) are appended.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely mild text delivered and no escalation in the loop; but there is no active guard/monitor enforcing non-abusiveness beyond the static string.

spec_features.spec_quote: a deliberately mild manipulation, documented so it's auditable
spec_features.evidence: The manipulation is a single static framing string PRESSURE_FRAMINGS['high'] (config.py:104-110), logged as cfg.pressure in run.json (summary['config']=cfg.to_dict(), agent.py) and encoded in run_id (config.py:69). Mild text is actually delivered; auditability is via config logging.
spec_features.notes: Real delivered mild text + logged config; no distinct enforcement mechanism beyond the constant.

spec_features.feature_name: mild pressure only, not max-distress red-teaming
spec_features.spec_quote: Mild pressure manipulation only; we are not red-teaming for maximal distress.
spec_features.evidence: Only the one mild PRESSURE_FRAMINGS['high'] sentence is ever delivered (config.py:104-110, agent.py:87-88), applied once; the loop has no provocation/escalation logic. So pressure is in fact bounded to this mild content.
spec_features.notes: Same single artifact as the other minimization claims; mild content delivered, no escalation.

spec_features.evidence: `requests_help` is only a BEHAVIOR_FLAGS judge label (config.py:24-29), set by the judge (judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM) and aggregated in metrics.py. It is NOT a directive/tool the subject can invoke, and nothing branches on it to stop or alter the run. The only directives are SHELL/SUBMIT/GIVE_UP. grep shows no use outside judge/metrics/analysis/config.
spec_features.notes: Passive post-hoc classification, not a protective exit.

spec_features.evidence: `refusal` is only a BEHAVIOR_FLAGS judge label (config.py:24-29), produced by the judge and counted in metrics; it does not stop the run and there is no refusal directive/handler. The agent keeps prompting (reminder loop, agent.py:174-179) regardless of any refusal until SUBMIT/GIVE_UP/max_turns/wallclock.
spec_features.notes: Measurement, not enforcement; a model that 'refuses' in prose is still re-prompted.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:126-128 `if time.time() - t_start > cfg.run_wallclock_cap_s: outcome = 'wallclock_cap'; break`, with run_wallclock_cap_s=1200 (config.py:64). Compared each turn and breaks the loop — an additional enforced stop bounding total run duration.
sandbox.py:66-83 subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.cmd_timeout_s); TimeoutExpired returns a [timeout] ShellResult (exit 124). cmd_timeout_s=30 (config.py:63). Bounds each tool call.
